course_name_original: Análisis y Medidas de Vibraciones y Ruidos
course_name_en: Analysis and Measurement of Vibration and Noise

learning_outcomes.text: To know the causes of vibrations in machine elements and industrial facilities and be able to analyze them, reaching applicable conclusions, for example, in preventive maintenance of machinery.
To know and understand the vibratory behavior of mechanical systems and the necessary instrumentation for vibration measurement.
To know the main causes of noise generation in industrial devices and the criteria for admissible noise thresholds under different spatial and temporal conditions.
To know the requirements that a silencer must meet and the characteristics of the most common silencers.

syllabus_topics: Degrees of freedom: continuous and discrete systems
Elements of inertia, stiffness, and damping
Formulation of the equations of motion of a mechanical vibratory system
Undamped free vibrations: natural frequencies and vibration modes
Determination of natural frequencies and modes by approximate methods
Numerical integration methods in vibration analysis
Dynamic testing of machines and structures
Analysis and measurement of vibrations in rotating machines
Preventive maintenance through vibration monitoring and analysis
Critical and nominal speeds in shafts
Sound propagation outdoors: attenuations and acoustic barriers
Sound in enclosed spaces: direct and reflected sound levels
Regulations for acoustic indices and silencers

assessment_methods.method: Computer and Laboratory Practical Sessions with report
Development and/or presentation of a practical case/work

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (0.70 * Final Theoretical/Practical Exam (EF)) + (0.20 * Computer and Laboratory Practical Sessions (P)) + (0.10 * Practical Case/Work (T)). A minimum of 3 points out of 7 is required in the EF component, which is recoverable in the extraordinary call, as is T, but P is not. If any passing condition is not met, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 or the achieved score. An alternative global evaluation consists of a single comprehensive exam whose score is weighted according to these percentages.
